message.content:
Below is a quick‑look calendar of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a Friday‑to‑Sunday stretch that contains at least one statutory holiday (or an observed holiday when the actual date falls on a weekend).  

| # | Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if needed) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---|---------|-------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Observed Monday Jan 2 | **Jan 1 – 3** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 2 | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | — | **Feb 18 – 20** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 3 | Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | — | **Apr 7 – 9** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 4 | Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | — | **May 20 – 22** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 5 | Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Observed Monday Jul 3 | **Jul 1 – 3** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 6 | Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | — | **Sep 2 – 4** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 7 | Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | — | **Oct 7 – 9** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 8 | Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 | Observed Monday Nov 13 | **Nov 11 – 13** (Fri‑Sun) |
| 9 | Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | — | **Dec 23 – 25** (Fri‑Sun) |

> **Quick notes**  
> * **Provincial variations** – Some provinces (e.g., British Columbia’s “St. Patrick’s Day” or Saskatchewan’s “Saskatchewan Day”) have their own holidays that can create additional long weekends.  
> * **Observed holidays** – When a statutory holiday falls on a weekend, the next weekday is usually observed. That’s why Canada Day (Sat Jul 1) and Remembrance Day (Sat Nov 11) are celebrated on the following Monday.  
> * **Boxing Day** – Although Dec 26 is a statutory holiday, it falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does not create a long weekend by itself.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app, and let me know if you’d like province‑specific long weekends or any other details!
